anomalies.observed: The CAN termination network is cross-wired through the 2-bit DIP switch: R34, which is tied to /CAN0_N, connects to SW6 pin 1; R35, which is tied to /CAN1_N, connects to SW6 pin 2; /CAN1_P is on SW6 pin 3; and /CAN0_P is on SW6 pin 4. With the standard two-row DIP-switch pin mapping, this places each 120 Ω termination resistor on the opposite CAN bus, and with an alternate pin pairing it directly bridges the N-side and P-side nodes of the two buses.
anomalies.expected: Each termination switch should connect its own 120 Ω resistor across its own CAN differential pair: R34 to /CAN0_P and R35 to /CAN1_P, keeping CAN0 and CAN1 independent.
anomalies.impact: Closing SW6 cross-couples or shorts the two CAN buses, causing CAN communication errors and defeating the intended separate/isolated CAN0/CAN1.

anomalies.observed: All WS2812B VSS pins are on Net-(D18-VSS), and that net connects only to Q10 pin 3 (drain). Q10 is an NMOS with pin 1 (gate) and pin 2 (source) both tied to GND, so VGS is zero and the device is off; the LED VSS node is therefore not connected to ground.
anomalies.expected: WS2812B VSS must be tied to GND, or a ground switch must be actively turned on. An NMOS with gate and source both at GND cannot provide the LED ground return.
anomalies.impact: The onboard addressable status LEDs cannot light because their ground return is floating.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23. It is not connected to +3V3, to a switched 3.3V supply, or to any other source node.
anomalies.expected: The common LED anode net should be connected to +3V3 or an intended switched 3.3V supply so the LEDs can be driven.
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet/activity LEDs connected to this net remain dark because their supply node is floating.
